What the library gives you

Four pieces, each one a thin layer over the standard library.

Typed lookups

Classes are the keys

Provide an instance and it registers under its own class. Look it up by that class and the static type survives, under mypy and pyright alike.

  • {{ check() }} use(Config) is inferred as Config
  • {{ check() }} Nested providers shadow, then restore on exit
  • {{ check() }} A miss falls back to set_default, then default=
{{ mockbar("config.py") }} 
@dataclass
class Config:
    url: str = "sqlite://"

with provider(Config(url="postgres://prod")):
    handler()

def handler() -> None:
    cfg = use(Config)     # -> Config
    print(cfg.url)
Injection

Parameters that fill themselves

Annotate a parameter and @inject resolves it from the active context at call time. An argument you pass explicitly always wins, so tests need no providers at all.

  • {{ check() }} The plan is built once, at decoration time
  • {{ check() }} Works on async def, methods, classmethods
  • {{ check() }} Generators are rejected instead of going stale
{{ mockbar("report.py") }} 
@inject
def report(cfg: FromCtx[Config] = injected):
    return cfg.url

with provider(Config()):
    report()                    # injected

report(Config(url="sqlite://"))  # explicit
Concurrency

Across tasks and threads

asyncio inherits the context on its own. Plain threads do not, so two helpers close the gap: one binds a callable to a snapshot, the other is a pool whose workers see the submit-time context.

  • {{ check() }} Sibling tasks stay isolated from each other
  • {{ check() }} Executor is a ThreadPoolExecutor subclass
  • {{ check() }} Worker writes never leak back to the submitter
{{ mockbar("jobs.py") }} 
with provider(Config()):
    Thread(target=wrap(job)).start()

    with Executor(max_workers=4) as pool:
        pool.submit(job)   # sees Config
Errors

Misses that explain themselves

A missing provider names what was asked for, lists what is active, suggests the close match, and points at the line you forgot to write.

  • {{ check() }} NoProviderError subclasses LookupError
  • {{ check() }} The key and the active keys are attributes
  • {{ check() }} frozen=True turns callee writes into errors
{{ mockbar("traceback") }} 
NoProviderError: use('datbase'): no active
provider for 'datbase'. Active providers:
'cache', 'database'. Did you mean 'database'?
Hint: did you forget `with provider('datbase')`?
